answer: Residual-Latency Trellis Audit: each agent answers randomized peer probes; residuals are plotted on a shared latency trellis. Clones sharing a scheduler create a synchronized knoll (correlated lag spikes) and a variance ledge across probe pairs, revealing duplication. Linked identities are quarantined. To evade, an attacker must give every clone distinct hosts, clocks, and probe-serving paths, multiplying infrastructure and monitoring cost.
